title: Finland Opens Criminal Case Over Google Data Center Forest Clearing

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Finnish authorities have opened a criminal investigation into the suspected environmental damage caused by Google at two AI infrastructure sites in the northern part of the country. The probe targets the illegal felling of an estimated 400,000 trees and the alteration of waterways and topsoil without mandatory environmental impact assessments. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority previously ordered a halt to construction at sites near Muhos and Otanmäki after finding the company had started work before receiving required permits.

The projects are part of a €13 billion AI investment, the largest of its kind in Finland. Google has apologized, stating it believed it was complying with the law, and has pledged to replant 130 hectares of forest. The incident has sparked national outrage, with a petition for stricter land use regulations and community fees attracting more than 93,000 signatures.

selectedTweets.text:
🦔Finnish regulators ordered Google to pause work on two data center sites after it cleared forest without the environmental impact assessments the law requires. The Finnish Society for Nature Conservation puts the count at about 400,000 trees across Muhos and Otanmäki. Google apologized and says it will replant 130 hectares. The two sites are part of a €13 billion AI investment, the largest of its kind in Finland, and more than 93,000 Finns have signed a petition for stricter rules and a fee paid to local communities.

My Take
If a Finnish landowner skipped the environmental review on a job this size, I doubt an apology and some replanting would close the case, and so far that’s about all Google has to deal with. I want foreign money to build in Finland. I also want the permit rules to apply to Google the same way they’d apply to a family that owns forest outside Oulu, and right now I can’t find any fine at all. 

People in Muhos have reason to feel shortchanged. Construction brings in a lot of workers for a couple of years, then the site runs with a small staff, and Google books most of its profit outside Finland anyway. The town deals with the trucks and the muddy creek now and doesn’t see much money later. I think some version of the community fee passes before the April election because it’s an easy win for politicians, and once Finland charges one, I’d expect Sweden and Norway to face the same pressure, since they sell data centers on the same cheap power and cold air. Google can pay a fee like that easily, but I’m not so sure about the smaller builders that finance their sites with debt.

Hedgie🤗
